text:
Sofia: Quick sync — we need to pick an ordered rollout for the Optimize toolkit (quantization, batching, caching). Customers pushing quantization, infra says batching is highest unit-cost win. Can we do a fast RICE-style call and surface launch criteria by EOD?

Kevin: I can run a back-of-envelope RICE now. Want impact = tokens saved / latency gains, reach = % of traffic, confidence = how sure we are about numbers, effort = engineering months.

Janet: Customer signal: two large customers requested quant to reduce GPU spend; both said they'd accept small quality regressions if we provide eval harness + fallback.

Corey: From infra ops POV: batching requires changes in serving runtime + autoscaler. Effort medium, but impact is immediate on cost for synchronous gen workloads. Caching depends heavily on workload shape — for chat apps it can be very high.

Kevin: Draft RICE (quick):
```
Quantization: Reach=0.4, Impact=3.0, Confidence=0.6, Effort=3.5 -> RICE~20
Batching: Reach=0.9, Impact=2.5, Confidence=0.8, Effort=2.0 -> RICE~90
Caching: Reach=0.5, Impact=2.8, Confidence=0.5, Effort=1.5 -> RICE~47
```
(rough numbers, just to orient sequencing)

Sofia: Interesting — batching jumps out from this quick pass. But we should factor launch risk + customer commitments. Quant has higher sales momentum.

Janet: Sales ask: if we do quant first we can close 2 pilot deals this quarter (revenue + feedback). If we delay, might lose those pilots.

Corey: Counterpoint: batching baseline reduces cost for everyone and is lower risk to model quality. Also easier to A/B flag.

Sofia: Proposed compromise: 1) Ship a minimal batching pilot (auto-batcher + metrics) targeted at high-throughput routes within 6 weeks. Launch criteria: 10% median token cost reduction on pilot traffic, no latency tail regressions >5%. 2) Parallel work: caching PoC for prefix-level cache for conversational flows — gating on hit-rate >15% in pilot. 3) Quantization: run closed beta for select customers with eval harness + automatic fallback to FP model on quality regressions.

Kevin: I like the parallel path. Suggest we attach explicit success metrics so PMs can trade-off. Also add rollback criteria for quant (delta vs baseline eval suite).

Janet: For sales: I'll promise pilots for quant beta if we deliver the eval harness + docs within 4 weeks. That buys time while batching pilot lands.

Corey: Need infra tickets: continuous-batching, autoscale-sla, cache-store-design, quant-eval-infra. I'll open them and tag owners.

ops-bot: Created 4 tasks: INF-842, INF-843, INF-844, INF-845 (linked in channel) :white_check_mark:

Sofia: Final ask — PMs, ops, and eng leads: agree to this sequencing? If so I'll write proposal and RICE appendix for review.

Kevin: SGTM :thumbsup:

Janet: SGTM, will coordinate customers for quant beta.

Corey: SGTM, will prioritize batching infra work in next sprint.

Sofia: Thanks all — I'll drop the proposal in #product and request async sign-off before EOD.
